la:adj:obustus.html:
ŏbustus, a, um, Part. [ob-uro].
Lit., burnt around, burnt, hardened in the fire (poet.): hic torre armatus obusto,: sudes,.—
Transf.: glaeba gelu,burnt by frost..

la:verb:obumbro.html:
ŏb-umbro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to overshadow, to shade (poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf.: opaco, obscuro).
Lit.: gramineus madidam caespes obumbrat humum,: coma umeros obumbrat,: templum,; Jahn (al. inumbret): sibi,to shade itself,: obumbratus amnis,; ; .—
Transf.
To darken, obscure: obumbrant aethera telis,: nubes solem obumbrant,.—
In gen., to cover over: germina obumbrata,.—
Trop.
To overcloud, darken, obscure: nomina,: candorem aequitatis,.—Prov.: sapientia vino obumbratur,; cf.: fidem amittunt propter id, quod sensus obumbrant,. —
To cover, cloak, conceal, disguise, palliale; to screen, defend, protect: crimen,: simulationem lacrimis,: magnum reginae nomen (eum) obumbrat,.
